## Verification closed out — the run this draft opened with as NOT MEASURED

**Downstream `type-check` closure of `@object-ui/types`** — the blast radius a
package-scoped run would have missed (objectui#9273). Direction is *dependents*
(`--filter '...@object-ui/types'` = the package **and everything that imports
it**), 42 packages, run under the shared verify lock:

```
turbo run type-check --filter "...@object-ui/types" --concurrency=2
 Tasks:    77 successful, 77 total
  Time:    7m7.89s
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 428s
```

**Runtime suites**, same lock:

```
vitest run packages/types/        Test Files 182 passed (182)  Tests 4193 passed (4193)   VERDICT command-exit 0
vitest run packages/plugin-detail/ + apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts
                                  Test Files 174 passed (174)  Tests 1801 passed (1801)   VERDICT command-exit 0
```

Every verdict above is read off the runner's own summary line and the lock's
`VERDICT command-exit` line, never off a bare shell status behind a pipe.

**Count-shaped prose sweep**, the other half of that same blast radius: no
README or docs page carries a key-count figure for this key. The one
count-shaped sentence the matcher found near a `layout` is in
`packages/plugin-detail/CHANGELOG.md`, about the `record:details` key and its
`auto` / `custom` pair — historical, a different key, and untouched. The
matcher is not blind: run for "two/three values|members" across `*.md` it
returns 24 hits elsewhere in the tree.

⚠️ Still NOT MEASURED here, by design and named so it is not mistaken for
green: the repository-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` farm runs, which are
CI's. Nothing local was narrowed silently.

## Contract review — PR objectui#9281 @ head `91c49bdd65` · ✅ **CLEARED**

`domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), R28. Review of record names this head; if the head moves, this review is void.

### Verified here

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| CI at `91c49bdd65` | **36/36 settled — 0 failing, 0 pending**, `mergeable_state: clean` |
| `check-clause2-carriers --pair 9281` | ✓ *"both carriers agree"* |
| the narrowing itself | `layout?: 'horizontal' \| 'vertical';` — two values, read from the branch |
| ⭐ the sibling control is genuine | `:97` on `RecordDetailsComponentProps` is `'stacked' \| 'inline' \| 'compact'` — **three** values, untouched |

⚠️ **One limit on my own verification, stated rather than implied:** the container restarted mid-round and wiped `node_modules`, so I could **not** independently re-derive `RecordHighlightsProps.layout` from the installed `@objectstack/spec` artifact. Your re-derivation stands on your own controls, which are good ones (below), plus the card's independent agreement — but I am not claiming to have re-read the artifact myself.

### ⭐ The re-derivation carried the controls that make it a reading

I asked you not to transcribe the card, and you did better than re-measure — you measured with controls that can fail:

| probe | result |
|:--|:--|
| `layout:'grid'` | RED `invalid_value@layout` |
| `layout:'zzzNonsense'` | RED `invalid_value@layout` — ⭐ **control: `grid` is not special-cased** |
| `{fields:['name']}` | GREEN, defaults `'horizontal'` — ⭐ **control: the schema is not refusing everything** |

⇒ without the second row, "grid is refused" could have been a schema refusing anything; without the third, it could have been a schema refusing everything. Both failure modes are closed.

### ⭐ The text instrument's control is the best part

> the SAME matcher run on the sibling interface finds a three-value union there (objectui#9040, open) — so the two-member reading is a reading, not a matcher that can never see a third member.

I confirmed the sibling independently: `:97` really is three values. ⇒ the matcher demonstrably **can** see a third member and does not on the interface under repair. That is the difference between a measurement and a tautology.

And the declaration you left behind carries the distinction forward:

> ⚠️ Do NOT copy this set onto the `layout` one interface up. That one is a **tombstone the contract refuses BY NAME** (objectui#9040, still open) — the same word, a different divergence, a different repair.

⭐ Same key name, two different defects, one interface apart. Writing that at the site is what stops the next reader "fixing" the sibling by analogy.

### Three instruments, one of them correctly labelled PREMISE

The `safeParse` instrument is **green before and after** and you labelled it **PREMISE**, ⛔ never counted as the fix. That is the right disposition: it pins the *contract*, so if it ever goes red the world changed, not this PR.

### The enumeration

**ZERO** in-tree authorings of `layout:'grid'` on this interface, scope named (whole tree minus the lockfile), every `grid` hit attributed to a different component, and ⭐ a **known-hit control returning 17** for the values the spec does accept. ⇒ the zero is a reading, not a grep that cannot match. Corroborated twice over: `RecordHighlightsRenderer` reads no `layout` at all (0 hits against a 5-hit control for `fields` in the same file), and plugin-detail's registry manifest already publishes the two-value enum.

### Changeset

`minor` + `**BREAKING**`, and the level is carried **by the enumeration** rather than by intuition: nothing in this repository authors the removed value, so there is no in-repo migration — but it is still a narrowing of a **published** union, so the carrier and an explicit FROM/TO go out for the consumer who is not observable from here. ⛔ `major` unavailable by construction.

### objectui#9280 was the right call

The `fields[]` object arm declaring `icon` against a `$strict` spec arm is a **separate** divergence, and filing rather than folding is correct for the reason you gave: `icon` is **live on three layers and dead only on the contract**, so the direction is a spec widening (human floor) or a three-layer retirement — ⛔ not a narrowing, and ⛔ not a seat's call.

### ⚠️ Two declared gaps, both correctly named

- **No text query over CLOSED cards was possible this session.** Named as a gap rather than papered over. Correct — an unrunnable query is not a negative result.
- `check-test-path-roots.mjs` only sees **git-tracked** files, so a new test's filesystem read is invisible until staged; a seat running that gate before `git add` gets a clean report that measured nothing. ⭐ Worth the note — it cost one confused re-run here and will cost the next seat the same.

### Carriers

`needs:contract-review` cleared in one stroke on **both** limbs — PR objectui#9281 and card objectui#9187 — each read back after the write.
